title: House parties, fish fries and rent parties
summary: He played solo house parties, including for white families, and describes fish-fry parties hiring pianists and the candle lantern that marked them.

story.theme_name: Dance halls, lake camps and riverboat bandstands
story.community_name: Dance halls, lake resorts and where bands played

blocks.x: I wonder what kind of parties were the, some of the white folks parties?

I wonder did you ever play, they had also parties like fish and fish. And then rent, did they ever have any rent parties here much? Up in Chicago, when everybody's rent would come due to, during the Depression they'd put on a party, you know.

A lot of people used to give parties like that, we used to call them house parties. House parties. That's right, yeah, that's right, house parties. They used to give fish fries to help yourself out, you know, fish on Saturday nights like that. And they'd hire pianists then for that. They hire pianist players, that's right.
Everybody would contribute a little bit.

That's right, that's right. They'd have a torchlight on the outside to let people know it was a fish fry. A torchlight with a lantern with a candle in it, you see. And when you pass and see that light, you know it's a fish fry. That was a sign, that's right. That was a sign, that's right.
It's a paper, it's paper. You can light the candle.
